LESSON: WRITING 6.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.4: Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you make others want to read your composition?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use appropriate words and expressions such as similes, metaphors, fixed phrases, phrasal verbs and idioms in written communication
2. create a pictorial composition from visuals

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 6.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 6.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use appropriate words and expressions such as similes, metaphors, fixed phrases, phrasal verbs and idioms in written communication

What this means
In this part you learn to use appropriate words and expressions such as similes, metaphors, fixed phrases, phrasal verbs and idioms in written communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use appropriate words and expressions such as similes, metaphors, fixed phrases, phrasal verbs and idioms in written communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use appropriate words and expressions such as similes, metaphors, fixed phrases, phrasal verbs and idioms in written communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create a pictorial composition from visuals

What this means
In this part you learn to create a pictorial composition from visuals. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a pictorial composition from visuals.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a pictorial composition from visuals. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use appropriate words and expressions such as similes, metaphors, fixed phrases, phrasal verbs and idioms in written communication)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing to a partner. (skill: create a pictorial composition from visuals)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use appropriate words and expressions such as similes, metaphors, fixed phrases, phrasal verbs and idioms in written communication.
3. Practise this skill: create a pictorial composition from visuals.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you make others want to read your composition?
2. What information do we obtain from pictures or visuals?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use appropriate words and expressions such as similes, metaphors, fixed phrases, phrasal verbs and idioms in written communication.
5. Be able to: create a pictorial composition from visuals.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
